b: Last week, I noted that Yesteryear had been pushed out of the top five—but that didn’t last long! It has climbed its way back into the #5 spot this time around. Sarah J. Maas is no longer in the #1 spot. Can you guess which title overtook A Court of Splintered Harmony? Here’s a hint: it was published in 2025.
Two New Books Out This Week You Should Know About
Unfortunately, the most read books on Goodreads tend not to be diverse by any definition of the word. So, here are a couple of new books out this week that deserve wider readership.
For the Love of K-Dramas by Lyla Lee

The behind-the-scenes drama is just as compelling as the on-screen in the world of K-dramas. When Clara Kim gets her big break on a new romantasy show, she’s laser-focused on succeeding. But her co-star, Shin Min-joon, might ruin her chance. Min-joon has criticized Clara on social media in the past. Since they’re thrown together for this job, they focus on understanding each other and making the chemistry look real. —Julia Rittenberg
In Your Skin by Aditya Bidikar, illustrated by Som

Never have I seen a book with a description involving “Bollywood body horror” before this one, and I am heartily intrigued. Not only that, but in this age of parasocial relationships, I’m kind of surprised we haven’t seen the IRL version of this play out. It starts with Priyanka, who has grown up watching Bollywood starring Ayesha San all her life. She’s seen all the movies, and knows every step to all the dances. When she gets the chance to meet the Bollywood star, Priyanka’s life gets a wrench thrown in it: Ayesha is retiring. Priyanka has a solution to Ayesha not wanting to live right, though; she’ll just take over her life… —Erica Ezeifedi
The Most Read Books on Goodreads This Week

Back in the top five is Yesteryear, which came out in April. It’s one of several buzzy tradwife novels out this year. In this one, a tradwife influencer wakes up one day in the time period she’s been romanticizing, and real-life homesteading turns out to be much more difficult—and dangerous—than it looks on Instagram. Yesteryear was read by almost 21,000 users this week and has a 3.8 average rating.

The fourth book in the Empyrean series still doesn’t have a release date, so fans likely have a long time to wait. In the meantime, they can revisit the world in this new novella, which follows 13 characters on their Threshing Days, when they endure a deadly trial in attempts to bond with a dragon. It was read by 21,000 users this week and has a 4.4 average rating.

The reigning queen of thrillers is back, this time with an October-appropriate story. After losing her job, Julia moves in with her elderly grandmother in their family’s 17th-century estate in Massachusetts. Soon, she begins to suspect the house is haunted by a woman executed for witchcraft in 1692. It was read by 24,000 users this week and has a 4.0 average rating.
A Court of Splintered Harmony (A Court of Thorns and Roses #6) by Sarah J. Maas

Sarah J. Maas is the author of 11 of the top 50 most read books this week, and the latest A Court of Thorns and Roses book is her most popular of the moment. It’s the first in the Valkyrie Cycle, following the Night Court as they face off against the return of Koschei the Deathless. The next book in the Valkyrie Cycle comes out in January. This one was read by almost 46,000 users this week and has a 3.8 average rating.
Sunrise on the Reaping by Suzanne Collins

This prequel novel in the Hunger Games series was published in 2025, but it’s getting new interest ahead of the movie adaptation, which came out November 20th. It follows Haymitch’s Hunger Games, 24 years before the events of the first novel. It was read by almost 50,000 users this week and has a 4.5 average rating.
